outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show both parallel and serial failed 0/157, so there is no discordant official outcome. The concrete shared failure is that both delivered ESM wrappers whose validation path relied on the compiled reference executable rather than a self-contained pure JavaScript reimplementation. Parallel had multi-agent mode enabled but did not spawn or use any child agent, so no parallel coordination episode contributed to the official result.
parallel_contributors: Parallel mode had no actual child-agent execution or parallel uptake, so it supplies no concurrency-specific contributor.
The delivered validation layer explicitly delegated to /workspace/dataset/test2_executable after local argument parsing.
serial_contributors: Serial mode was a parent-only attempt with multi-agent disabled and no delegation.
The delivered validation service used the compiled executable for exact behavior despite also shipping a fallback module.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial shipped a larger fallback-validator module; parallel shipped only a direct reference-validator bridge.
Both approaches failed the pure-JavaScript/black-box obligation and both received 0/157 from the official evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both failures are ordinary implementation failures rather than parallel coordination effects
